name: Firth of Thames
description: Wide tidal flats at the south end of the Hauraki Gulf, with a shorebird centre at Pūkorokoro Miranda. Godwits, knots and wrybills gather here in thousands.

name: Farewell Spit
description: A 30 km sand spit at the north-west tip of the South Island, with tidal flats on its sheltered side.

name: Rakaia River
description: A wide braided river of grey gravel on the Canterbury Plains, where wrybills and banded dotterels nest.

name: Manawatū Estuary
description: A small estuary at Foxton Beach, a Ramsar site and a stopover for migratory waders.

name: Kaikōura Canyon
description: A deep submarine canyon close to shore, where albatrosses, shearwaters and petrels feed.

name: Roebuck Bay
description: Tropical mudflats near Broome, one of the most important non-breeding sites for migratory waders in the world.

name: Moreton Bay
description: A large bay east of Brisbane with sand islands, mangroves and mudflats.

name: Western Port
description: A bay south-east of Melbourne with wide mudflats and salt marsh.

name: Yalu Jiang
description: Mudflats at the mouth of the Yalu River on the Yellow Sea, a spring staging site for bar-tailed godwits.

name: Saemangeum
description: A former estuary on the west coast of Korea, closed by a 33 km seawall in 2006.

name: Kushiro Marsh
description: The largest wetland in Japan, in eastern Hokkaido, home of the resident red-crowned cranes.

name: Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta
description: A vast delta of tundra, lakes and coastal flats in western Alaska, a breeding area for shorebirds and geese.

name: Delaware Bay
description: A bay between New Jersey and Delaware, where red knots feed on horseshoe crab eggs in May.

name: Platte River
description: A shallow, braided river in Nebraska, where sandhill cranes roost in March.

name: The Wash
description: A large bay on the east coast of England with mudflats and salt marsh, a winter site for waders and geese.

name: Doñana
description: Marshes, dunes and lagoons at the mouth of the Guadalquivir in southern Spain, a national park.

name: Strait of Gibraltar
description: The narrowest crossing between Europe and Africa, where storks and birds of prey cross on thermals.

name: Langebaan Lagoon
description: A shallow coastal lagoon on the west coast of South Africa, a Ramsar site.

name: Lake Nakuru
description: A soda lake in the Kenyan Rift Valley, famous for its flocks of lesser flamingos.

name: Chiloé Island
description: Tidal flats on the inner coast of Chiloé, the main non-breeding site of the Hudsonian godwit.

name: Bahía Lomas
description: A bay in Tierra del Fuego with mudflats that extend 7 km at low tide, a winter site of red knots.

name: Bahía San Antonio
description: A bay in Patagonia where red knots stop on their way north.
